---
title: "Research pipeline"
---

The procedural research code is organized in **`review/`**, separately from the inference package `PRESS/`. It prepares the observations, fits the five components, composes held-out h and xLoss, and produces the descriptive reports. The implementation is being reviewed before the final package release; this page provides its reading order and input/output layout.

## Numbered workflow

The [execution plan](review/00_pipeline.py) prints the commands in dependency order. The task scripts retain the same simple organization: definitions of covariates or likelihood, training and validation, then a pipeline that executes those steps.

| Step | Component | Reading order |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | Preprocessing | [Preparation](review/preprocessing/features.py) → [pipeline](review/preprocessing/pipeline.py). Tracking derivatives and segmentation are in [tracking.py](review/preprocessing/tracking.py); pass links are in [passes.py](review/preprocessing/passes.py). |
| 02 | Expected threat | [Model](review/expected_threat/model.py) → [training](review/expected_threat/training.py) → [pipeline](review/expected_threat/pipeline.py). |
| 03 | Physical ball-drive risk | [Model and priors](review/ball_drive/physical/model.py) → [training](review/ball_drive/physical/training.py) → [pipeline](review/ball_drive/physical/pipeline.py). |
| 04 | CatBoost ball-drive comparison | [Features](review/ball_drive/catboost/features.py) → [training](review/ball_drive/catboost/training.py) → [pipeline](review/ball_drive/catboost/pipeline.py). |
| 05 | Pass probability | [Physical model](review/pass_probability/model.py) → [training](review/pass_probability/training.py) → [pipeline](review/pass_probability/pipeline.py). |
| 06 | Pass selection, flat and cross-nested | [Features](review/pass_selection/features.py) → [training](review/pass_selection/training.py) → [pipeline](review/pass_selection/pipeline.py). |
| 07 | Action selection, then residual risk | [Features](review/binary_classification/features.py) → [training](review/binary_classification/training.py) → [pipeline](review/binary_classification/pipeline.py). |
| 08 | h, xLoss and band evaluation | [Composition](review/composed_risk/features.py) → [scores and bootstrap](review/composed_risk/scores.py) → [pipeline](review/composed_risk/pipeline.py). |
| 09 | Possession patterns and reports | [Classification](review/reports/features.py) → [scores](review/reports/scores.py) → [real-frame cases](review/reports/cases.py) → [pipeline](review/reports/pipeline.py). |
| 10 | Statistical summaries | [Parameter and performance tables](review/benchmarks.py). |

Flat and cross-nested pass selection share their feature calculation. Action selection and residual risk also share feature definitions, but their models, labels and outputs remain separate. The physical ball-drive model remains the deployed one; CatBoost is a benchmark comparison.

## Inputs and outputs

```text
review/
  00_pipeline.py
  frame_states.py
  inputs/                         # local numerical inputs, by task
    shared/tracking/matches/<id>/
    preprocessing/matches/<id>/
    expected_threat/
    ball_drive/
    pass_probability/
    pass_selection/
    binary_classification/
    composed_risk/
    reports/
  <component>/                    # source files in the table above
  outputs/                        # a new run's generated objects
    preprocessing/
    expected_threat/
    ball_drive/physical/
    ball_drive/catboost/
    pass_probability/
    pass_selection/flat/
    pass_selection/cnl/
    binary_classification/action_selection/
    binary_classification/residual_risk/
    composed_risk/
    reports/
    statistics/
  local_history/initial_run/       # local only; never exported
```

Each model stores feature tables or physical arrays separately from fold fits, scores and production refits. Saved trees, spline bases, posterior quantities and calibration objects have explicit task folders. The pipelines refuse to replace completed outputs silently. The [input/output guide](review/README.md) describes the individual files.

The raw-data adapter reads the public SkillCorner match files. Shared preprocessing retains the broad observations and quality flags; task-specific outcome filters remain beside the task. Reconstructed task cohorts are saved under `outputs/preprocessing/task_inputs/` and compared by observation keys and labels before replacing accepted inputs. Segmentation and context-label meanings are explained in the [User guide](vignettes/setup/possession_and_checkpoint_setup.ipynb).

## Dependencies between models

Fold-specific feature builders receive explicit upstream model artifacts from the matching split. They do not search previous experiments or substitute production models for held-out evaluation. Accepted upstream inputs are stored under `inputs/<task>/upstream/fold_<f>/`; production counterparts are under `upstream/production/`. The numbered plan runs the reviewed task procedures from these declared inputs; it does not automatically promote newly generated experimental fits into downstream inputs.

For the six-fitting/two-validation/two-test tree-model splits, physical and xT features use the matching fitting data; pass-completion and pass-selection calibration retain their declared validation roles. Residual-risk training uses cross-fitted P(carry); validation and test use the corresponding main action-selection model. Production residual training uses the five eight-fit/two-held action fits. The [general benchmark](benchmark.qmd) and individual benchmark pages describe these procedures.

BCOS quantities used in the accepted benchmarks and pretrained classifiers come from the **preliminary formulation with effective hazards**. The [updated transport-with-killing formulation](vignettes/spatial_features/bcos/10_bcos.ipynb) is presented mathematically; its implementation, numerical comparison and downstream retraining belong to the planned package revision. The current pipeline preserves the benchmark feature definition.

## Composed risks, bands and reports

The composition stage produces one held-out h and xLoss per verified canonical checkpoint, using the models of the fold in which the match was held out. It fits no additional predictor or calibrator.

- Overall h/xLoss metrics and calibration use **15,085 verified-outcome states**.
- Bands, possession patterns and player/team reports use **14,919 states from 7,265 possessions** with terminal canonical-action coverage.
- Band intervals resample whole matches, with 2,000 replicates, fixed predictions/thresholds and seed 20261030. Empty and nearly empty bands are checked explicitly.
- Player/team E−O scores resample whole individual possessions. The reports also provide pattern shares and exposure/retention summaries with their stated denominators.
- Case studies retain real match/possession keys and use the package's frame plotting function. A later verified control illustrates the outcome without adding a canonical checkpoint.

Details and results are in the [composed-risk benchmark](benchmarks/06_composed_risk.qmd) and the [pressure report](vignettes/07_case_studies/07_case_studies.ipynb).

## Local checks

The [verification plan](review/checks/run.py) covers syntax and command-line entry points, reconstruction of a real match, physical calculations, short model fits, serialization, composition, metrics and report counts. The [check guide](review/checks/README.md) distinguishes these tests from a new scientific benchmark.

For pass selection, the [short real-data check](review/checks/pass_selection_steps.py) retains the complete destination grids for ten observed passes. It exercises flat/CNL likelihoods and gradients, the declared curvatures, reduced screening, tree and nesting updates, early stopping, temperature scaling, held-out scoring, feature importance and model export. Full training grids remain cluster work.

```bash
# Print the ordered research commands without executing fits.
python review/00_pipeline.py --output-root /path/to/new_run

# Print local checks; add --execute to run selected checks.
python review/checks/run.py --output /path/to/new_checks
```

## Release contents

The [release script](review/release.py) uses an explicit file allowlist. Alongside the source code, the site exposes statistical summaries of physical parameters, performance/calibration, bands and selected case-study/report tables. Full input tables, feature matrices, fold boosters, posterior objects and bootstrap replicates stay local. Pretrained inference models remain distributed with the PRESS package.

The initial historical run has separate scripts, inputs and outputs under `local_history/initial_run/<task>/`. It is retained locally and is not a dependency or part of the public export. Experimental runs are also excluded. Nothing in this research workflow installs new weights into the package automatically.
